text: {"question":"How do the two studies use CMB observations to constrain physics beyond the standard cosmological model, one by examining the evolution of the effective number of relativistic species and the presence of self‑interacting light relics, and the other by employing a simplified four‑parameter model of inhomogeneous reionization?","reference_answer":"Both analyses rely on CMB data to test extensions of the standard model: the first probes variations in the radiation density and perturbation dynamics through Neff evolution and self‑interacting relics, while the second constrains the ionization history via a compact reionization parametrization that captures the main CMB signatures of inhomogeneous reionization.","passage_1_contribution":"The study uses LBT and CMB data to search for light relics with strong self‑interactions and to test consistency between radiation densities inferred from both probes.","passage_2_contribution":"The work adopts a four‑parameter reionization model that approximates inhomogeneous reionization effects on the CMB, enabling tractable constraints on the ionization history.","joint_reason":"Both passages illustrate how CMB measurements can be leveraged to constrain non‑standard physics—one through radiation density evolution and perturbations, the other through modifications to the ionization history—highlighting complementary approaches to probing early‑universe phenomena.","same_quantity":false}
